source.original_title: 05/16/2026 - Luis Ortiz & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/16/2026 - Luis Ortiz & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Closed

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'You, you spoke with Kim, I think, right?' Prospect: 'Yes, we spoke that, I think it was on, I think it was Thursday.' Confidence is medium rather than high because the prospect separately called the setter 'Kevin' ('Like I was talking to Kevin about') and referred to them as 'he' ('He gave you me some notes'), so either the prospect did not retain the setter's name or the setter identified themselves differently on the phone. May also be transcription noise.

prospect.name: Luis Ortiz
prospect.location: Los Angeles, California, USA; originally from a small ranch in Mexico
prospect.occupation: Sales lead — recruiting, staffing and some HR across multiple properties, required to be on site as 'the face of the company'; works Monday through Sunday. Previously an elementary school physical education teacher, then a school librarian during his recovery.
prospect.family_status: Sister (married); grandmother in Mexico; girlfriend not mentioned for him. Mentions friends and family he wants to influence.
prospect.training_background: Long-distance runner and marathoner, rebuilt from one mile to 13-15 miles after his accident. Adult-league baseball, park basketball, training camps, martial arts when young. Daily step count was at least 33,000, now 'drastically dropped'. Describes himself as lean and deliberately not bulky. Vegan for over five years, now vegetarian. Owns kettlebells already and started self-directed kettlebell work from online programmes before stopping.
prospect.medical: Struck by a car at an estimated 30+ mph while walking on the sidewalk, thrown 20+ feet through a wooden gate. Broken collarbone, bone bruising on both heels, knee, back and neck injuries. Six months on crutches then six months on a cane; extensive physical therapy; roughly two years to recover mobility and strength. Was told he would not run again. A second car accident roughly two years ago aggravated the original trauma. Current: ongoing neck pain from above the shoulders to the edge of the head, left shoulder pain and upper mid-back pain, all on the left side where he took the original impact. Also tweaked an ankle about a year ago, managed with bands. Describes contralateral compensation and feeling 'unaligned'.

signals: Lost ground to a catastrophic injury and a punishing job, and wants a former self back: 'if I did it before, I could still do it again'
Carries explicit regret about the recent slide: 'I put too much emphasis in this job, and I kind of just became a workhorse... I think I've let myself go because of that'
Frames the purchase as restoration plus refinement, not rescue: 'it's kind of like making sure that I'm getting polished up, like I know I had a little hiccup, and I need to get back on it'
Not the_prehab_fighter: the health events are in the past and he is recovering from them, not training through an active one

goals.text: Gain mobility and be pain-free, particularly in the left shoulder, neck and upper back
Get lean and defined — biceps, cut core, build muscle without bulk
Build muscle while staying flexible, agile and quick
Get back to being as active as he was, when his daily step count was 33,000+
Return to baseball, basketball and running now that the job has squeezed them out
Become the best version of himself as a whole-lifestyle change — 'pretty much becoming a new, a new person'
Learn enough to help friends and family and be someone people follow

pains.text: Chronic post-traumatic neck, left shoulder and upper mid-back pain from being hit by a car, aggravated by a second collision two years ago
Body compensating to the opposite side, feels 'unaligned' and is overworking the wrong muscles
Works Monday through Sunday, sometimes eight-plus hours on site or travelling site to site, and is now desk-bound where he used to be on his feet
Activity has collapsed from 33,000 steps a day to almost nothing; now out of breath climbing a couple of flights of stairs
Guesses at his own programming — searches online for kettlebell exercises, starts a programme, then stops
No accountability or expert feedback since his physical therapist; nobody to tell him whether his form is right
Loses motivation because there is no defined end goal: 'not having that end goal at the end of the day, not knowing how this is going to change'
Trauma from the collision and the hospital discharging him the same night unable to walk, the day before his sister's wedding

objections.raw_quote: I have, uh, some, I was not expecting 6k, but I was expecting someone, I know above 3k easy, not saying it's not, you know, but, um, I had something, an idea of how much it was going to be and not saying it's not worth it.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it cleanly — 'do you feel like we can actually help you money aside? That's the most important bit, right?' — then ran a worth-it reframe: 'six months down the line, if all this does is get you paying free, let's say, and just teach you everything, it's worth it.' Prospect agreed it was worth it 100%.

objections.raw_quote: as like I said, I could put it in the credit card, but right now, like I owe some things that I got to pay off. Um, so, I mean, once I get that paid off, like, well, at least where it covers the, well, I'm able to get the 6k.
objections.rep_response: Isolated again ('Is there anything else that's holding you back, or is it just that?'), then structured a payment plan live: 50% down and the balance within 90 days. Quoted a three-payment alternative at 3 x $2,300 and advised against it. Then offered Klarna and asked his credit score.

objections.raw_quote: As far as like, you know how you were saying the check-ins every week, or like pretty, how would that take place, like through Zoom calls?
objections.rep_response: Told him there are no calls: 'we have an app, we don't do any calls, we don't really, we found that we used to, but we don't really need them, and it ended up just being a waste of time.' Then softened it with a personal offer: 'I would jump on with you. I've done it for people before where I've said I'll jump on with you once a month.'

offer.payment_plan_terms: Agreed: $3,000 down, remaining $3,000 within 90 days, total $6,000, no surcharge. Rep also quoted an alternative of three payments of $2,300 (total $6,900, an added $900) and actively steered away from it: 'I'd just do it in two, if I was being honest'. Klarna was then offered as a monthly-instalment route after the rep asked his credit score.

prospect_financials.note: Disclosed outstanding credit card debt he needs to pay off before he could cover $6,000 outright. Had anchored his own expectation at somewhere above $3,000. No cash-on-hand figure, no monthly surplus, no card count or available credit was asked for.

evidence: Explicit verbal agreement after considering Klarna: 'You know what, no, I think I'm just gonna, I think I'm gonna just go for it. Let's do it dude.'
Payment collection was actively under way on the call — rep screen-shared Stripe, took the prospect's email (luortiz89 at gmail.com) and began entering the charge
Terms settled before the yes: $3,000 down with $3,000 inside 90 days, total $6,000

Counter-evidence: the recording ends at 00:52:25 with the rep saying 'Let me turn the recording off though, because I don't want to accidentally record your information.' Payment success is therefore not evidenced on the transcript, and the onboarding steps after it are unverifiable. Treated as closed on the strength of the verbal yes plus a payment flow in progress, not on a confirmed receipt.
outcome.next_step: Onboarding Zoom call with Trevor booked for the following day; tailored training, nutrition and mobility plans to follow 24-48 hours after that, so 'by Tuesday or Wednesday'.

notable.note: Highest-risk clinical profile in the batch and it was never screened. The prospect was hit by a car at 30+ mph, thrown 20+ feet through a gate, spent a year on crutches and a cane, was told he would never run again, had a second collision two years ago, and still has active left-sided neck, shoulder and upper-back pain. He was sold a programme whose first described workout is 'swings, into snatches, into push-ups as a circuit' — overhead ballistic loading straight onto the injured side — and no one asked whether any clinician had cleared it. The rep's response to the disclosed compensation pattern was 'you've probably got some imbalances, dude, but it's fine. We'll fix it.' Separately: the rep made an unprompted claim that people of Indian descent have 'worse genetics when it comes to fitness'; he repeatedly used the prospect's near-fatal collision as a joke, including as a payment-close line; and he quoted a three-instalment option at $6,900 against a $6,000 list price. On the credit side, the commitment check at 00:42:33 was the cleanest in the batch and was correctly run before any number was named.

quality.notes: Severe. The prospect is labelled 'luort' and long stretches are inverted: the entire offer walkthrough from roughly 00:30:25 to 00:33:28 is attributed to 'luort' but is plainly the rep, and the whole price quote and payment-plan negotiation between 00:44 and 00:51 alternates wrongly, with prospect questions landing under the rep label and vice versa. The block at 00:12:59 opens under 'luort' but contains the rep's 'would you be able to make 30 minutes a day four days a week'. Roles read from content throughout.
